subject.title: fix(exec): validate script files outside the workspace root for shell bleed

question: Should outside-workdir script operands be subject to the same shell-bleed preflight as in-workdir scripts, even though existing direct exec commands may start failing on shell-style `$VAR` tokens?
rationale: The patch closes a real skip in a security-sensitive exec preflight path, but it deliberately changes runtime behavior that current main and the adjacent test currently allow.

options.title: Accept bounded hardening
options.body: Land the stricter outside-workdir validation as an intentional security hardening and own the compatibility effect for scripts containing shell-style tokens.

options.title: Preserve old compatibility
options.body: Keep the outside-workdir skip by default, or require a separate maintainer-approved strict mode before blocking these commands.

options.title: Pause for owner review
options.body: Leave this PR open until the exec/security owner decides whether this bypass justifies the behavior change.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded hardening
recommendation.body: Land the stricter outside-workdir validation as an intentional security hardening and own the compatibility effect for scripts containing shell-style tokens.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and merged the original shell-bleed preflight behavior, making them the strongest history-backed owner for this compatibility/security tradeoff.
